function: Over-the-air aggregation of FedAvg local weight vectors over OTFS, using zero-forcing delay-Doppler precoding, optimal per-device power allocation, and EKF channel tracking to cut CSI exchange (pp. 1, 4).
system: Five mobile IoT devices and one server, single-antenna (scalar delay-Doppler channel, p. 3); OTFS uplink, M=32, N=64, 3.75 kHz spacing (p. 5); no RIS; band not stated.
method: Federated learning (FedAvg) of an unspecified classification model; aggregation uses a closed-form zero-forcing precoder, Lagrangian power allocation, and an extended Kalman filter, none learned (pp. 4-5).
data_channel: Simulated extended vehicular A (EVA) channel, parameters from [14], Gauss-Markov path-gain evolution (pp. 4-5); task data: MATLAB nnet toolbox synthetic handwritten digits 0-4 (p. 5).
test_conditions: Training and testing share one simulated five-device setting; separate FedAvg runs per maximum velocity (120, 200 km/h) and SNR (10-50 dB); channel MSE for gamma 0.9, 0.995 (p. 5).
baselines: FedAvg over OFDM (conventional OTA-FL, no reference given) and FedAvg over an ideal no-fading channel as upper bound; no baseline for the channel tracker (p. 5).
metrics: Test classification accuracy of the global model versus communication round; MSE between true and EKF-reconstructed delay-Doppler channel versus SNR (p. 5).
complexity: Orders reported: EKF O(Lk^2.4) per device, ZF precoder O(MN^2.4), optimal power O(MN); CSI shared drops from MN to 3Lk samples (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 5: "The simulations are performed with an extended vehicular A (EVA) model." EVA is a standardized 3GPP LTE profile outside the listed models; see notes.
q2_support: p. 5: "(c) Accuracy of the global model against number of iteration of FedAvg under varying maximum velocity of IoT devices"; each velocity and SNR is a separate FedAvg training run, so no trained model is tested in an unseen condition.
q3_support: p. 5: "we plot the accuracy of classification of the model when CS and IoT devices employ OFDM for communications"; this OFDM scheme cites no earlier aggregation design and the ideal channel is only a bound, so no published learned baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 5: "The complexity involved in the computation of ZF precoder Pk can be determined as" O(MN^2.4); the EKF costs O(Lk^2.4) and the power allocation O(MN).
q5_support: p. 5: "train a classification model using the dataset supplied by the neural network (nnet) toolbox of MATLAB"; this is a learning-task dataset, the channel is simulated, and no code or data link is given.
notes: Over-the-air FL work: the precoder, power allocation and EKF are not learned, so it passes no_learning only through the over-the-air FL rule. Area 7 rather than 4 because the problem solved is the over-the-air aggregation itself and the main metric is global accuracy. The server and devices are single-antenna (scalar channel, p. 3; p. 1 contrasts with the multi-antenna server of [9]); kept because OTFS works admit single-antenna links. Reviewer: confirm this exception covers an area-7 OTFS work; otherwise the reason is system. q1: EVA, the extended vehicular A profile standardized by 3GPP for LTE (TS 36.101/36.104), is not among the listed models; the paper does not name 3GPP, and path gains also follow a Gauss-Markov evolution (p. 4). Reviewer to confirm. Fig. 2 legends (p. 5, read from the page image): Proposed Scheme (OTFS), FedAvg over OFDM, Ideal Channel. Carrier frequency not stated. Title and DOI on p. 1 match.
